 Australia seal thrilling win over England in first T20 - as it happened
 21 November 2026 Sat 21 Nov 2026 , Men's International Twenty20 Match - 1st T20I Australia vs England, result Australia Australia Result England England 191 -7 ( 19.5 ) 187 -9 ( 20.0 ) Australia   win by 3 wickets Australia innings: 191 for 7 from 19.5 overs
 England innings: 187 for 9 from 20.0 overs
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 First of five T20s, Melbourne
 Australia chase MCG T20 international record target of 188 to seal win by three wickets off penultimate ball
 Aus 191-7 (19.5 overs): Chaudhary 66 (38), Marsh 37 (32)
 Eng 187-9 (20 overs): Brook 65 (28), Banton 39 (22)
 Second T20 at Gold Coast on Tuesday
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter
 Get involved Live Reporting
 by Timothy Abraham & Matthew Henry
 Join us on Tuesday... published at 12:11 GMT 12:11 GMT 
 That's your lot from the MCG as Australia take a 1-0 lead in the five-match T20 international series with a dramatic three-wicket victory with one ball to spare.
 Be sure to read Matthew Henry's report before you leave us... 
 We will back with coverage of the second T20 which is being played at the People First Stadium in Carrara on the Gold Coast in Queensland next Tuesday. 
 That one is an 08:15 GMT start and we will have live-text commentary on the BBC Sport website with ball-by-ball coverage from the TMS team out in Australia.
 Here's the best of sandpapergate stories to read between now and then:
 Lehmann again denies knowing about sandpaper plot 
 Cummins' integrity not compromised - CA 
 Cummins' Australia captaincy at a crossroads - Agnew 
 The sandpaper plot - who was there, who said what? 
 Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins 
 2 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'The future of Australia...' published at 12:05 GMT 12:05 GMT 
 Australia skipper Mitch Marsh: "It's been a pretty crazy 12 days [with sandpapergate]. Today we saw the future of the Australia side with those young guys and hopefully we can get back to enjoying that.
 "They are a great bunch. We haven't spent a lot of time together but I could tell they were excited. There were a few nerves in and around the group but I want them to not care about making mistakes, enjoy the environment and have the confidence they belong."
 On dropped catches: "I was a little bit worried when we dropped the best batter in the world a few times! Most of the time you don't deserve to win but I thought outside of a few chances the energy and the speed [in the field] was great to watch. They are all good kids. They are the future. It's really positive signs."
 7 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 12:01 GMT 12:01 GMT 
 Jason Gillespie 
Former Australia bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 I'm pleased for Jack Edwards. He was great there in that last over.
 17 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 '10 runs more and we win...' published at 12:01 GMT 12:01 GMT 
 England captain Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation: "A very entertaining game of cricket to go down to the last few balls. It's what the fans wants to see, and everyone watching on television. We were probably 10 runs short of what we needed on that surface. 
 "The pitch got better and the dew came in to make a bit of a difference. If we had 10 more runs we probably win the game. Unfortunately we were on the wrong side but hopefully everyone enjoyed it.
 "Liam Dawson and Adil Rashid are wily operators and it's awesome to have those two in the middle. Liam was outstanding in the powerplay as well to pick up a couple of wickets and almost swing the momentum our way."
 20 24 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:57 GMT 11:57 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Player of the match Nikhil Chaudhary, who took 2-21 and made 66 off 38 balls: "It's always good to play for Australia and especially at home. There's nothing better than playing at the MCG and winning this game. 
 "My parents came over from India last night so nothing better than getting a player of the match in front of them which is their first game her watching me.
 "With the ball, Joel Davies gave me the idea with the lines and lengths to bowl. I got the big wicket of Harry [Brook] to start. Batting, it's a big game against England and you just have to stay stable and keep playing your game at the crease which was I did."
 33 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 11:52 GMT 11:52 GMT 
 Highest successful run chases by Australia at home:
 191-7 v England, Today
 173-8 v South Africa, Cairns 2025
 161-4 v South Africa, Brisbane 2009
 32 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'An amazing game...' published at 11:50 GMT 11:50 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images England captain Harry Brook speaking to BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra: "We were a little bit under-par. It was an amazing game, to go down to the last couple of balls, it was exciting.
 "In the past we've done really well in these tight games. We had 10 too few runs - with 10 more, we would've won the game.
 "T20 is such a fickle game, we've got to bounce back as quickly as possible. You've got to bank these experiences, learn from them and move on.
 "I'm just happy I managed to get a few out of the middle. I should've got a few more."
 52 36 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 11:48 GMT 11:48 GMT 
 Australia have completed a record chase at the MCG, eclipsing the 172-5 made by Sri Lanka against them at the ground in a T20 international 2017.

Ex-Australia coach on Test Match Special 
 Fantastic result. Well played Jack Edwards and Nikhil Chaudhary will be man of the match.
 The young guys didn't panic at all.
 The batter of the night was still Harry Brook, though. It was incredible to watch.

 Full from Sam Curran and Jack Edwards square drives it for four through backward point.
 Australia win by three wickets.

 Sam Curran winds up the MCG by tying up his laces at the top of the mark. Booes ensue.
 Jack Edwards drills the left-arm seamer for a couple.

 Harry Brook and Sam Curran have a long debate about the field. England bring all their fielders up.
